import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io

# Prepare the data from the string input
csv_data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and visually appealing style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a figure-level plot (catplot) to show the relationship between
# passenger class, sex, and survival rate. This is a very insightful
# visualization for this dataset as it highlights the stark differences in outcome.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    kind="bar",
    x="class",
    y="survived",
    hue="sex",
    palette="viridis",
    height=7,
    aspect=1.5,
    legend_out=False,
    order=["First", "Third"]  # Order based on the available data
)

# Access the underlying axes for further customization
ax = g.ax

# Add a clear, descriptive title and labels
ax.set_title("Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex", fontsize=20, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel("Passenger Class", fontsize=16, weight='bold', labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel("Survival Rate", fontsize=16, weight='bold', labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to show percentages for better readability
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f'{y:.0%}'))

# Add data labels on top of each bar to show the exact survival rate
for p in ax.patches:
    ax.annotate(f"{p.get_height():.1%}",
                (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                ha='center', va='center',
                xytext=(0, 10),
                textcoords='offset points',
                fontsize=12,
                color='black')

# Customize the legend
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', frameon=True, shadow=True)

# Adjust layout to prevent title/labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close()
